title: Triage-to-Close Sellframe — visual notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick visual cheat notes for a 6–8 slide sellframe that moves an integration from initial triage to a closed pilot commitment. Intended for SEs and platform sellers running 15–30m technical discovery + exec alignment.

TL;DR (one-liners to lead with)
- Why: show pragmatic route from technical triage -> measurable pilot -> contract (reserved cap or hosted uplift).
- Outcome: reduce friction by aligning on 3 pilot success metrics (latency p95, cost/token, accuracy on eval set).

Audience: integration architect, infra/platform lead, product owner, procurement (late).

Visual decision ladder (core concept) — single-slide idea:
- Row of stakeholders left->right: Integration Engineer -> Platform Architect -> Product Owner -> Security/Compliance -> Procurement/Finance
- For each stakeholder show one key question and one artifact they need to sign off:
  - Engineer: "Will it integrate?" -> repo + quick curl demo / sample latency traces
  - Platform: "Will it lock into infra & SLAs?" -> topology diagram + routing policy options
  - Product: "Does it move KPIs?" -> success metric baseline + A/B plan
  - Security: "Is data secure?" -> KMS/HSM + audit log summary
  - Procurement: "Cost predictability?" -> pilot pricing path + reserved capacity options

Slide-by-slide skeleton (6–8 slides) — speaker notes for each:
1) Opening (30s) — The problem + 1-sentence value prop
  - Line: "Reduce inference cost while keeping SLA and output quality"
  - Quick evidence: "customer X cut gen cost 32% with batching + caching" (callout: replace with actual case)
2) Quick topology + integration surface (1–2 min)
  - Minimal requirements: outbound HTTPS, 2 routes for canary, optional VPC peering for private deploys
  - Show sample call flow (client -> model routing -> cache layer -> response)
3) Pilot design (core) — scope, duration, success metrics
  - Suggested scope: 2 weeks staging, 4 weeks pilot in prod-like env, 1 cust engineer + 1 SE
  - Success metrics (pick 3): p95 latency < X ms, token cost <$Y per 1k, quality > baseline by Z% on eval set
4) Fallback & reliability strategy (ops-centred)
  - Canary routing: 80/20 split -> auto-fallback to smaller quantized model on latency breach
  - Suggested error budget SLOs and alerts to instrument (p99 errors, queueing depth)
5) Security & compliance snapshot (one-liner per control)
  - Data residency, KMS integrated, audit logs, optional private control-plane
6) Commercial sketch (pilot pricing + paths)
  - Self-serve hosted credits -> pilot discount -> reserved commit conversation (show ballpark ranges)
7) Objections & rebuttals (battlecard compact)
  - Objection: "We can self-host cheaper" -> Rebuttal: TCO includes SRE dev time; show break-even calc (2–3 bullets)
  - Objection: "Latency unpredictable" -> Rebuttal: p95 statistics + routing + dedicated capacity option
8) Next steps / Decision ladder (call-to-action)
  - Clear asks: technical kickstart sheet, sample dataset, AP contact + date to run first load test

Compact battlecard (one slide to carry into calls) — top lines to memorize:
- One-line positioning: "Redwood Inference = predictable inference with dev-friendly ops: low latency, lower unit-cost, enterprise controls."
- 3 quick wins to promise: quick curl demo in <30m, measurable cost delta in 2 weeks, canary + fallback ready
- 5-second rebuttals for common objections: self-host, vendor lock-in, model quality, security, procurement

Pilot telemetry checklist (data SEs must collect) — table snippet (columns described):
- metric: token throughput, p50/p95 latency, cost/token, success-rate (business metric), model-output accuracy (eval)
- baseline value, pilot target, collection query (log path)

Operational playbook (brief)
- Pre-run: validate sample traffic shape with loadgen (script in repo -> link to PR-321)
- Canary: 10k requests/day ramp with 5-step ramp, rollback trigger = sustained p95 > threshold for 5m
- Post-run: compare eval set outputs vs baseline and annotate regressions (tie to Redwood Optimize alert)

Sample scripts & lines (copyable) — include in slide notes
- Quick curl to hosted API (placeholder): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"<sample>"}'
- Can run small curl in demo env to show streaming and partial tokens

Commercial knobs to flex during negotiation
- Capacity: burst vs reserved; pricing discounts scale nonlinearly (show three tiers)
- Model variants: cheaper quantized model for high throughput vs larger model for quality-sensitive endpoints
- Observability add-on: extended retention for token-level traces (useful for audits)

Quick objection cheats (short scripts)
- "How do you handle model regressions?" -> "We ship evals + canary rollouts and automatic fallback; we can run your eval corpus during pilot to baseline."
- "What about cost predictability?" -> "Reserved commits or per-route quotas + token-level billing exports for forecasting."

Open questions / TODOs (for this doc)
- Insert real 3rd-party case study numbers (ask CS: GT-3289 for permission)
- Get confirmed pilot pricing ranges from finance (Aisha)
- Add latest latency charts from infra (Tom) — link to SLO dashboard (placeholder)

Appendix (short)
- Sample pilot timeline (Gantt-like): Week 0 (kickoff + dataset), Week 1 staging tests, Week 2 start canary, Weeks 3–4 data collection + adjustment, Week 5 decision
- Short checklist for kickoff call: dataset access, API keys, contact matrix, success metric definitions, rollback criteria

Notes-to-self style (rough):
- Keep slides very visual: one diagram per slide, minimal bullets
- Keep pricing as ranges, not committed numbers in initial talk
- This doc should live with /link to pilot-run-template (confluence) and a one-click demo env (ops link)

Feedback requested from: Tom (latency charts), Aisha (pricing), Diego (security checklist).
